Results.ReviewText: I've had this grill for a little more than three years, and it's an incredible value. I can do darn near anything on this grill, from burgers, steaks and chicken to pizza and low and slow barbecue. One thing I would recommend would be to buy a roll of grill gasket. I installed some gaskets around the lid, and it's made a huge difference on the amount of heat the kettle will hold. I'd usually top out around 500 degrees with a couple chimneys of briquettes, and that would fall and level off at 400 pretty quickly once I opened the lid. Now, it consistently peaks at over 600 and consistently stays above 500 with two full chimneys.

Results.ReviewText:
This is my 4th Weber kettle over the past 30 years.  They are my favorite grills.  I've used each one until it fell apart.  Here's my review of this one.

Pro's:

- This is my first kettle that has the bracket to hold the lid when the grill is open.  I like that much better than the hook that was inside the lid of my previous kettles.
- I like the handles and the handle on the lid vent much better.  My previous kettles had wood handles that rotted and nothing insulated on the lid vent, so I would have to open and close that with an oven mitt.
- I like the warming rack.  Never had one before.  It's really nice for getting food farther from the heat.
- I like the new shape of the cutouts in the one-touch cleaning system.  It provides more precise control over air intake into the grill, and thus the grill's internal temperature.

Cons:

- My #1 con is the new ash catcher design.  It's much harder to reattach after emptying, and there's enough of a gap that plenty of ashes fall out on the ground, even when the ash catcher is empty.  Epic fail as far as I'm concerned.
- The cooking grate, with the separate center section that can be taken out to use accessory cooking devices.  I have no interest in using other devices (I have all the accessories to do all that already), so this is nothing but an annoyance for me (the center grate falls out whenever I remove the grate - like to start a fire.  It also has a tendency to flip and fall through the grate when I'm cleaning the cooking grate with a brush).  I dislike this so much that I'm going to spend more to get a solid cooking grate.

Frankly, if I had it all to do again, I'd have bought another original kettle.
Results.Title: Some improvements and some shortcomings

After years of checking out YouTube channels such as Babyback Maniac, TRoy Cooks, How to BBQ Right, etc. and listening to these guys talk about Weber Kettles, I decided to take the plunge when my previous charcoal grill finally gave up the ghost.  

Right out of the box, it worked better than I had hoped.  I seasoned the grill by cooking high fat hamburgers on it a few times, then I put it to work smoking.  I added a gasket around the lid, just to help with heat retention.  I also went and purchased a digital thermometer with two probes.  One for grate temp and other for internal temp of meat.  Still getting used to how to dial in temp but I can't complain.  I used a 2X1 snake method to smoke an 11lbs brisket and the charcoal lasted well over 16 hours without refilling.  I was even able to use last coal to start another pile to cook baked potatoes to have with brisket.

BUY THIS GRILL!!  You will not be disappointed!

14501001.Description: Some things never go out of style—like the smoky flavor of charcoal, the sizzle of a summer cookout, and the iconic silhouette of the 22" Master-Touch™ Charcoal Grill. This grill features a handy Tuck-Away Lid Holder that gives you a convenient place to nest the lid against the side of the bowl, a hinged cooking grate that fits circular GBS accessories so you can explore more ways to cook, a built-in lid thermometer, and legs that are 2” taller than standard kettles. Like all Weber® kettles, it’s built to last with a porcelain-enameled bowl and lid that retain heat and resist rust, peeling, and scratching, and adjustable lid and bowl dampers to fine-tune the heat for perfect results.
